evidence: Ov. Tr. 4.10.22: Maeonidēs nūllās ipse relīquit opēs
Cic. Tusc. 5.61: cōpiās ejus, opēs, majestātem dominātūs
terms.comment: Means of every kind: money, property, power (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.42: nē major benignitās sit, quam facultātēs

phrases.latin: saepe pater dīxit 'studium quid inūtile temptās? Maeonidēs nūllās ipse relīquit opēs'
phrases.english: my father often said, ‘Why take up something so useless? Homer himself left no money’

phrases.latin: Sunt quidem omnīnō nōbīs modicae facultātēs, dignitās sūmptuōsa
phrases.english: My means, it is true, are modest, and my position is costly

sources: Lewis & Short: ops · Lewis & Short: facultas · Lewis & Short: copia
